invariant: Java lowers every attached note to a synthetic leaf plus an ordinary Link. Degeneration is allowed only with zero groups and zero links. Bibliotekon maps any group endpoint to its cluster special point, and ClusterDotString emits that point whenever any SVEK edge, including a note link, touches the group. Semantic aliases remain metadata; Graphviz edges use concrete empty-leaf or cluster-special-point IDs.
causal_divergence: Rust's parser resolves package aliases correctly, but the renderer's notes-only shortcut ignores packages and generated note links. Attached-note edges use semantic package aliases instead of relationship_layout_id, so LayoutGraph drops them when no node has that ID. Nonempty package clusters create special endpoints only for ordinary relationships, not attached notes. The retained note slots are consequently never painted because their solved edge is absent.
planned_change: Restrict notes-only degeneration to the Java no-group/no-link shape; map attached-note package targets through relationship_layout_id for graph construction and solved-edge lookup; and create cluster endpoint nodes whenever either an ordinary relationship or attached note touches the package. Keep semantic aliases in SVG metadata and comments. Do not change parser target ownership or note-slot ordering.

scope_boundary: This mechanism owns class attached-note degeneration and semantic-to-layout endpoint routing for package targets. It does not alter package corner geometry, note typography, parser ownership, general edge routing, scaling, comparator behavior, baselines, or fixture eligibility.
